Murmuring to herself, Hadley said, “How could this have happened… Why did Linda collapse so suddenly?”

“What’s going on here?”

Today marked the Flynn family’s grand banquet, and the estate was bustling with guests. Those who heard the commotion quickly encircled Linda, who was sprawled out from her fall down the stairs.

“What’s going on? How did she end up falling?”

“Look up there. She…”

“You’ve crossed the line!”

“No, that’s not true…”

As the accusations flew, Hadley’s complexion turned pale, and she vehemently shook her head in denial. She tried to assert her innocence, insisting she hadn’t pushed Linda. However, her pleas fell on deaf ears.

“Make way!”

A commanding male voice disrupted the gathering, asserting his presence authoritatively.

That voice belonged to Eric Flynn, Hadley’s new husband, though their marriage had lasted only a brief period.

Hadley barely started to respond when Nyla turned her back and walked away.

Suddenly, the crowd began to thin out.

Ignored by everyone, Hadley found herself aimlessly returning to her room, lost in a fog of confusion.

the-tycoon-hidden-bride-her-ultimate-rev.description:
“Elliana, remember what I told you. Until you turn twenty, never show your beauty or your talents.”

For fifteen years, Elliana Marsh had lived by her mother’s final words. She kept herself plain and acted ignorant—just to blend into the background. But today was her twentieth birthday. She was ready to let go of the old Elliana and show the world her true self.

She filled the tub with warm water, added bath salts, and placed her makeup remover nearby. Just as she started undressing for a long, relaxing soak to wash off the ugly makeup, a loud knock shattered the peace.

Irritated, she threw on a robe and opened the door.

Melody Ahmed, the maid, stood there, her nose in the air as usual. “Elliana, what are you sneaking around in here for? It’s Miss Jones’s wedding day. If you don’t show up, people will start whispering and tarnish the Jones family’s image. Go to the front hall, now!”

Elliana smirked derisively. This maid had never been polite to her. The accusation of “sneaking around” was hardly accurate. In truth, she had been confined to the back room for fifteen years, ever since her mother’s death. After her mother’s passing, her stepmother, Kiara Jones, along with her father and Kiara’s illegitimate daughter, Paige Jones, had swiftly joined the Jones family and taken over everything.

The worst part? Not even her father, Darin Jones, treated her the way she deserved.

“I’ll go change,” Elliana said calmly.

Melody scoffed. “What’s the point? With that ugly face of yours, no dress can save you. Move it! The Evans family’s already here. The City Hall staff is on-site to register the marriage between Mr. Evans and Miss Jones. Mrs. Jones wants everyone present for the big moment.”

Elliana’s lips curled into a cold smile.

The Evans family was the most powerful in Ublento. Cole Evans, their heir, was a business genius. Paige was the city’s favorite socialite. Of course, their engagement had been all over the news. People called them a perfect couple, a match made in heaven. Every compliment in the book was used to describe them. Social media was going wild. Everyone was eagerly waiting for their grand wedding.

Kiara made it sound proper and grand, but Elliana knew the truth—she was simply dragged out to watch Paige shine.

Elliana changed quickly and followed Melody to the front hall.

The Jones family’s residence looked like a palace, decked out in over-the-top luxury to celebrate Paige’s big day.

Everyone in the room wore elegant outfits, except for Elliana. She stood out like a sore thumb in a cheap white T-shirt, ripped jeans, and hideous makeup. She didn’t just clash with the scene—she crashed it.

Kiara was chatting with Cole’s grandfather, Ruben Evans, when Elliana walked in. Kiara paused and then put on her usual fake smile. “Elliana, I got you a beautiful new dress. Why didn’t you wear it?”

Elliana inwardly rolled her eyes. As if Kiara ever did anything for her. She used to fake being clueless and play along with Kiara’s charade, but now she was done with these games. She didn’t bother replying to Kiara. Instead, she turned to Ruben and gave a polite nod. “Hello, Mr. Evans.”

Ruben chuckled. “Well, Elliana, you’ve certainly got your own style these days.”

Elliana ran a hand through her messy wig. She hadn’t expected him to be so tolerant. At least he wasn’t calling her a disaster.

Her eyes naturally drifted to the man beside Ruben. She’d noticed him the moment she stepped in. From his posture and presence, she could tell—this had to be Cole, the mysterious heir rarely seen in public. Seeing him up close was something else. Tall, sharp, and ridiculously handsome. He looked like he’d stepped straight out of a romance novel. She couldn’t help but stare just a little too long.

“Look at Elliana,” Melody sneered, her voice loud on purpose. “Ugly as hell, yet she dares to drool over Paige’s fiancé. What a joke. With that face, even looking at Mr. Evans is a crime.”

Melody was clearly following Kiara’s silent orders.

Paige leaned closer to Cole, clinging to his arm as though claiming her prize. “It’s fine. Cole’s amazing. It’s only natural that other women like him.”

Paige didn’t see Elliana as a threat at all. In fact, she wanted Elliana to chase after him. It made her feel even more superior—like she had already won.

Darin’s face twisted in anger as he snarled at Elliana, “What a disgrace. Get out of here!”

Elliana dragged over a chair with one leg and dropped into it casually, right across from Cole.

Cole didn’t flinch. His face remained blank, cold as stone.

Ruben cleared his throat awkwardly and turned to the City Hall staff members. “Let’s check if we missed any documents for the marriage registration.”

“Of course.” The City Hall members opened their laptops and checked for any missing materials. A moment later, one of them froze and looked at Cole hesitantly. “Mr. Evans… The system says you’re already married. Your wife is listed as Ms. Elliana Marsh.”

“Wait, what?” Gasps filled the room.

Elliana’s eyes went wide. Shock hit her like a slap. She was married?

And to Cole Evans, no less? But she had no idea how.

Her family didn’t care about her at all.

They only brought her back because Emily didn’t want to marry a vegetative man! It was pointless to say anything more.

“It’s not about the dowry.”

Sandra’s heart was already numb from the pain, so her expression didn’t change.

“I want to go to the hospital to see Emily.”

Kyle’s anger dissipated, and he looked at her with suspicion.

“Yes. Will you dare to let me?”

Joseph King is an American author celebrated for his emotionally layered storytelling, relatable characters, and the quiet power of his prose. Known for blending contemporary realism with heartfelt emotional depth, King has built a devoted audience who find comfort, truth, and reflection in his writing. His novels often explore human resilience, family bonds, regret, redemption, and the complicated beauty of second chances.
Born in Sacramento, California, Joseph grew up in a modest household where books were treated like windows to the world. His mother, a literature teacher, encouraged nightly reading, while his father—a bus mechanic—taught him the value of persistence and humble hard work. Joseph often says his imagination “grew up in the public library,” where he spent countless afternoons filling notebooks with characters and worlds long before he knew he wanted to become an author.
King attended the University of Washington, majoring in English Literature and Creative Writing. During college, he won the campus short-fiction award twice, and professors frequently praised his instinctive ability to capture emotion with simplicity and grace. After graduation, he worked as a freelance editor, bookstore assistant, and part-time writing coach, slowly building a foundation for his literary career.
His breakout novel, Silent Branches, brought him national recognition. The story—about a fractured family attempting to rebuild after a painful loss—earned acclaim for its authenticity and lyrical beauty. Critics called King “a rare voice capable of turning everyday moments into profound emotional experiences.” The novel inspired book clubs across the U.S., and King became known as a writer who could make readers feel seen, understood, and deeply moved.
Following the success of Silent Branches, King published Half-Moon Harbor and Where the Night Still Breathes, both of which cemented his reputation as one of America’s most beloved contemporary storytellers. His works have since been translated into multiple languages, and he frequently speaks at literary festivals, universities, and creative-writing workshops.
Despite his success, Joseph remains grounded. He lives in Seattle, Washington, with his wife and their golden retriever, Winston. When he is not writing, he enjoys hiking coastal trails, collecting vintage typewriters, and teaching young writers who dream of telling stories that matter.
Joseph King believes that every ordinary life holds extraordinary meaning—and through his writing, he continues to remind the world of the quiet strength within the human heart.
Chapter 1 — Summary 
Story: Wolf romance ? Fated rejection ? Awakening wolf



Part 1 — A Night Meant for Love, Not Ruin
Avery had waited her whole life for Mating Day — when wolves turn 19 and find their destined mate.
Even without a wolf form, she believed she and Ryan — the Alpha heir — were meant to be.
They planned to choose each other before fate could interfere, mark each other, and build a life of love and protection.
She even wore secret lingerie.
She even believed tonight would be magic.
Instead, she opened his bedroom door to a nightmare.



Part 2 — Betrayal in Bed
Ryan was naked —
but not for her.
Her younger half-sister Zara straddled him, smirking, moaning theatrically, digging her teeth into his neck like she was performing for Avery.
Avery froze.
Her life shattered in one instant.
Ryan’s excuse?
“We just found out we’re fated mates.”
The word fated cut like a blade.
Destiny chose Zara — the girl who bullied her, humiliated her, laughed at her wolflessness — to take everything.



Part 3 — A Heartbreaking Truth
Zara coiled around Ryan like a snake.
With every breathy moan, she branded him as hers.
Ryan said what Avery had always feared:
“Fated mates make each other stronger.”
Translation:
you were never enough.
She trembled, holding back tears:
“So I was nothing to you?”
Her voice cracked.
Her heart split.
Ryan’s wolf surfaced, gold flickering in his eyes.
“Get lost, human.”
Not even Avery.
Not even a name.
Human.
Like she was nothing.



Part 4 — Running With a Broken Heart
She ran.
Tears slicing her face.
Her lungs burning.
Her world collapsing.
She sprinted deep into the forest, to her secret pond — the one peaceful place she’d ever had.
Where she once dreamed about her future.
She hugged her knees, shaking in agony, the earth soaking up her grief.
But Mating Moon night is dangerous — restless unmated wolves roam, heated, violent, unpredictable.
And Avery was alone.
Heartbroken.
Wolfless.
Unprotected.



Part 5 — Awakening Heat
Then it hit her — a scent.
Wild.
Powerful.
Addictive.
Heat exploded through her veins like fire.
Desire, instinct, raw and primal.
She gasped — body trembling, breath catching.
Heat?!
She never had a wolf.
She could never shift.
She was supposed to be wolfless.
So why was she burning from the inside?
This scent… this pull…
It felt like a fated mate bond awakening.
Impossible.
Terrifying.
Overpowering.



Part 6 — Danger in the Dark
Before she could understand, figures emerged from the woods — rogues.
Men with knives, sweat, hunger — and interest.
They smelled her heat.
They saw vulnerability.
They circled her like predators.
“A female wolf in heat.”
She trembled.
Threatened, cornered, overwhelmed.
“Stay away from me!”
They laughed.
Predators amused by prey.
One grabbed her.
She choked on fear.
No wolf.
No power.
No backup.
Just a girl abandoned twice in one night — by her mate and her world.



Part 7 — The Breaking Point
They reached for her clothes.
Her tears spilled.
Her voice shook.
Her body wanted to collapse.
Everything in her screamed for safety.
For help.
For the wolf she never had.
And suddenly — a roar ripped through the night:
“LEAVE HER ALONE!”
A voice like thunder and command.
The intoxicating scent intensified — drowning out the rogues, drowning out pain, flooding her senses with instinct, heat, and safety all at once.
Her knees nearly buckled.



Part 8 — The Alpha Presence
He emerged — unseen yet terrifying, powerful and furious.
The rogues froze — fear slicing through them.
This wasn’t just any wolf.
This was dominance.
Command.
Danger — and salvation.
Avery’s body reacted beyond control — heat darkening her vision, pulse racing, breath sharp.
Whoever he was, he was the source of the scent.
The heat.
The awakening inside her.
Was he—
Her fated mate?
Impossible.
Yet her soul howled toward his presence.



Part 9 — A Wolf Awakens
Her wolf — once silent, mocked, “dormant” — stirred.
A growl echoed inside her mind.
Alive.
Awakening.
Claiming.
The forest held its breath.
Everything Avery ever believed — that she was weak, wolfless, unwanted — shattered in that second.
Her wolf wasn’t gone.
Just waiting.
Waiting for him.



Part 10 — A New Destiny Begins
One night.
One betrayal.
One scent.
One voice.
Her world flipped.
Ryan wasn’t her destiny.
Zara wasn’t her end.
Her wolf wasn’t dead.
A stranger in the dark was the spark — and the storm.
The rogues shifted nervously.
Avery trembled between danger and desire, heartbreak and awakening.
And when the stranger spoke again, the ground itself seemed to bow:
“Touch her — and I’ll tear you apart.”
A mate bond stronger than betrayal.
A wolf rising from ashes.
A fate rewritten under the moon.
Avery’s story of pain had just become her story of power.

“Sebastian is coming back?”
The eight-months pregnant Sasha was folding the newly bought onesies in the nursery when she heard the housemaids’ conversation. He’s coming back? Is it because my due date is approaching?
Her heart was bursting with joy until her hands trembled.
Although Sebastian was the baby’s father, she had only met him once on their wedding night. He never showed up after that.
With watery eyes, she caressed her pregnant belly. “Oh, my baby, I know your daddy doesn’t like me, but it’s okay. I will be happy as long as he’s here to witness your birth.”
A smile of joy and satisfaction lit up her face.
Two days later, Sebastian was finally back after disappearing for ten months.
When Sasha heard the news, she held her baby bump while carefully trotting out of her bedroom to meet him.
As she looked down from the top of the stairs, her face turned ashen. Apart from the man whom she missed a lot, she saw a woman standing next to him in the living room.
“Sebastian, I asked you to come back to take care of Sasha. Why did you bring this woman back?”
“Don’t you know why? I told you I have nothing to do with this marriage. The woman I want to marry is Xandra, and she’s standing next to me right now.”
In his black coat, Sebastian’s chiseled face held a frosty expression. The man exuded a cold aura while he levelled his father’s stare.
Frederick was left fuming at his son’s words. “Don’t you know Sasha’s due date is near? She’s pregnant with your baby! How dare you say something like that!”
“Huh,” he snorted, “The baby? She wouldn’t be pregnant if you hadn’t spiked my drink on my wedding night. You know what, the baby doesn’t deserve to come to this world!”
The living room fell into a dead silence.
Standing by the staircase, Sasha felt a dull pain from within her chest; his words pierced through her heart, tearing it to smithereens. At that instant, she experienced a temporary blackout of vision while the surrounding noises faded away. How could he say something like that! My baby… My baby is unwelcomed…
